$comment: VERSIONED CONTENT, NOT CODE (Carl, 12 Sep 2026; PRACTITIONER-QUEUE-PAGE.md section 3a; hard rule 14). THE FOUR STATES A VISIT CAN BE PUT IN FROM THE PRACTITIONER'S WAITING LIST. Carl's words: '1. With patient now 2. Pending (patient in queue) 3. Completed (consultation completed) 4. Reassign (to a different Doctor)'. This is a list a user picks from, so it is content and not a TypeScript union (CLAUDE.md section 7, first instance assignor-relationships.json): the list changes without a code change, the screen renders it in FILE ORDER, and the version travels onto every record it produces. THE DISPLAY WORDS ARE NOT HERE -- they live in the string table keyed by `key` (REQ-LANG-01/-02), because a translated word must never be able to change what a state MEANS.
$attendanceComment: IT IS ATTENDANCE, NOT CLINICAL DOCUMENTATION (section 3a rule 1; VISIT-CHECKLIST.md section 5). Who, what state, when -- and nothing else. There is no free-text field on this list and none on the record it writes, because 'a note box here becomes a clinical record within a week'. There is no reason, no triage, no duration and no amount (hard rule 4).
$neverGatesComment: NO STATE HERE GATES ANYTHING (section 3a rule 5, hard rule 8, REQ-REC-04). An unset state changes nothing about whether the patient is seen or billed, and neither does a set one. Every value below is a REPORT of what happened in the room.
$flagComment: WHAT THE THREE FLAGS MEAN. `settableByHand` -- may a person choose this from the control? Pending is FALSE: it is where every visit starts and nobody sets it, so it is shown as the current answer and never offered as a choice. `isTheServiceRenderedSignal` -- setting this is what tells the platform a service happened, which is what raises the post-service agreement (section 3a rule 3, VISIT-CHECKLIST.md section 6); exactly one option may carry it. `raisesAFrontDeskTask` -- setting this asks RECEPTION to do something and moves nobody (section 3a rule 4: 'Reassign never reassigns'); the covering-provider check and the re-papering are reception's, on the front desk page. The two act-flags are mutually exclusive: an option that both ended the visit and asked for it to be handed on would be two answers at once.
